An adult human body has 206 bones.
Babies are born with around 300 bones, many of which fuse later.
The femur (thigh bone) is the longest bone in the human body.
The stapes in the ear is the smallest bone in the human body.
More than half of your bones are in your hands and feet.
Noses and ears tend to look larger with age as cartilage and skin change.
Fingernails grow faster than toenails.
Hair grows roughly 1 cm a month.
You lose dozens of hairs every day — that's normal.
Your skin is your body's largest organ.
You shed millions of skin cells every day.
Your stomach lining renews itself every few days.
The small intestine is around 6–7 metres long.
Your heart beats around 100,000 times a day.
Blood makes a full circuit of your body in about a minute.
Red blood cells live for roughly 120 days.
Your blood vessels laid end to end would stretch tens of thousands of kilometres.
The left lung is slightly smaller to make room for the heart.
You breathe roughly 20,000 times a day.
Your brain uses about 20% of your body's energy.
The brain itself feels no pain.
Your brain has about 86 billion neurons.
Nerve signals can travel at over 100 metres per second.
Humans have more than five senses, including balance and body position.
Your eyes can distinguish millions of colours.
Each eye has a blind spot where the optic nerve leaves it.
You blink around 15–20 times a minute.
The cornea has no blood vessels; it gets oxygen from the air.
Your nose can tell apart a vast number of different smells.
Taste is strongly influenced by smell.
Umami is the savoury taste found in foods like tomatoes and parmesan.
Taste buds are replaced every couple of weeks.
Your tongue print is unique.
Fingerprints form before birth.
Identical twins have different fingerprints.
Humans are the only animals known to blush.
Goosebumps are a leftover reflex from when our ancestors had more body hair.
Yawning is contagious, even between people and dogs.
Laughing uses muscles all over your body.
Humans have over 40 muscles in the face.
The strongest muscle relative to its size is often said to be the masseter (jaw).
The gluteus maximus is the largest muscle in the body.
Muscles can only pull, never push.
Tooth enamel is the hardest substance in the human body.
Humans get two sets of teeth in a lifetime.
An adult has 32 teeth, including wisdom teeth.
Saliva helps start digesting starch before food reaches your stomach.
You produce about a litre or more of saliva each day.
Your liver can regenerate after part of it is removed.
The liver performs hundreds of different jobs.
You can live with one kidney.
Kidneys filter about 180 litres of blood plasma a day.
The appendix may help store helpful gut bacteria.
There are roughly as many bacterial cells in your body as human cells.
Your gut bacteria weigh around 200 grams or so.
Water makes up around 60% of an adult's body weight.
You're slightly taller in the morning than at night.
Sneezes can blast air out at high speed.
Hiccups are sudden spasms of the diaphragm.
Your ears help you balance, using fluid in the inner ear.
Earwax helps clean and protect your ears.
Humans can't breathe and swallow at exactly the same time.
Bone is living tissue that constantly breaks down and rebuilds itself.
Humans are good long-distance runners compared with many animals.
People who are left-handed make up roughly 10% of the population.
Dreams happen mostly during REM sleep.
Adults typically need around 7–9 hours of sleep.
Babies can't taste salt very well until a few months old.
Newborns can only see clearly about 20–30 cm away.
The human eye can detect a single photon under ideal lab conditions.
Human DNA is about 99.9% identical from person to person.
